audit.whatIsWrong: win[3] said Skill while whys[3] calls Levels 4-5 'your tank lane-control peak'; win[6] said K'Sante while whys[6] says 'Two-item Swain reclaims it'. The packet chart has K'Sante at 4-5 and Skill at 2+ items.
audit.why: Swain has no dash and a 12s root that only lands on the return pass, so 4-5 is genuinely yours; his drain plus permanent max-health stacking pulls the late back to level.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 = K'Sante, 2+ items = Skill, in matched full/content pairs.

audit.why: Lvl 3, Lvl 6, first item, late are correct; the late spike now names why it is his.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's entire answer to Nevermove was 'W's unstoppable charge lets you ignore his E root', repeated across whys[1], whys[2], spikes[0], early, mid and wants.you[0]. Unstoppable is not in Riot's text for Path Maker (it says 'charges up, taking reduced damage'), so the advice rests on a claim the kit cannot support.
audit.why: The real, checkable mechanic is better advice anyway: Nevermove launches a wave forward and roots only on its RETURN to Swain, and it is a projectile. So the play is to be out of the return line, not to tank the root with a status you may not have.
audit.corrected: Every 'unstoppable' line replaced with the return-pass read plus the 12s rank-1 cooldown.
sources: kit file: swain E text and projectile flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Ravenous Flock's healing and permanent max-health stacking were never named, and 'Demonic Embrace' was cited twice as his drain source.
audit.why: The sustain comes from Ravenous Flock's Soul Fragments and Demonic Ascension's drain; Grievous Wounds timing is what actually decides the extended fight, and stacking resistances alone does not answer permanent HP growth.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds written into whys[6], spikes[3] and late, with Ravenous Flock named.
sources: kit file: swain P heal/percentHealth flags

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere; the tracked ability was his ultimate rather than the root.
audit.why: Nevermove is 12s at rank 1 and Vision of Empire 22s — those are the windows you commit into, not his 120s R.

edits.before: At 2 you pick up W or E; W's unstoppable charge already lets you ignore his E root and step in safely.
edits.after: At 2 you pick up W or E; Nevermove only roots on its return pass, so step in and clear the second hit.

edits.before: Full Q-W combo online — W through his E pull voids the root, then Q3 knocks him up on a champ with no escape.
edits.after: Full Q-W combo online — sidestep Nevermove's return, then W and Q3-pull him; Swain has no dash to leave with.

edits.before: Two-item Swain reclaims it: his R + Demonic Embrace drain heals through your trades, so close before the long AOE fights start.
edits.after: Two-item Swain reclaims it: Demonic Ascension drains straight through your trades unless Grievous Wounds is already on him.

edits.before: Your full Q-W combo is online — charge W through his E pull so the root whiffs, then Q3 knock-up and walk him down.
edits.after: Your full Q-W combo is online — clear Nevermove's return so the root whiffs, then W in, Q3-pull, and walk him down.

edits.before: Two-item Swain in a teamfight is his peak — his R drain + Demonic Embrace heal off your whole team, so don't let a long AOE fight start on his terms.
edits.after: Two-item Swain in a teamfight is his peak — Demonic Ascension drains your whole team and Ravenous Flock banks it as permanent health, so bring Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: Level 1 is even — he pokes with Q and you just farm with Q tip, eating a little chip you can shrug off as a tank. The key from Level 2 onward is your W charge: it makes you unstoppable, so when he throws E to pull-and-root you, charge W through it and the root does nothing. Don't blow E (Footwork) to dodge his bomb early; save it to close the gap his slows leave on you, then Q3 to knock him up.
edits.after: Level 1 is even — he pokes with Q and you just farm with Q tip, eating a little chip you can shrug off as a tank. The key from Level 2 onward is reading Nevermove: the wave only roots on the way BACK, so walk through the outgoing cast and be out of the return line. Don't blow E (Footwork) to dodge his bomb early; save it to close the gap his slows leave on you, then Q3 to pull him in.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your peak. He has no dash and no escape, so once you W into him through his E and Q3, he's stuck eating your full combo and you out-trade his poke as a tank. At 6 be careful with All Out — it strips your bulk, and his W bomb plus R drain punish a squishier you, so ult to dash through and peel out, not to stand and facetank his AOE. Bait the E pull, walk it down with W unstoppable, then commit.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your peak. He has no dash and no escape, so once you W into him and Q3-pull, he's stuck eating your full combo and you out-trade his poke as a tank. At 6 be careful with All Out — it strips your bulk, and his W bomb plus R drain punish a squishier you, so ult to dash through and peel out, not to stand and facetank his AOE. Bait Nevermove's return, then commit while it is down 12 seconds.

edits.before: This is the window Swain wants. A two-item drain mage heals off your whole team with R and Demonic Embrace, and his E-pull engage starts long AOE fights where his sustain beats your trades. You're still a strong peeler — R to pull him off your carry or peel his — but don't let him start a sustained teamfight on his terms. Use your earlier-to-mid lead and your W to lock him down before his stacks and items make the drain unstoppable.
edits.after: This is the window Swain wants. A two-item drain mage heals off your whole team with Demonic Ascension, and Ravenous Flock turns those Soul Fragments into permanent max health, so Grievous Wounds is not optional. You're still a strong peeler — R launches him off your carry — but don't let him start a sustained teamfight on his terms. Use your mid-game lead and your W to lock him down before the drain out-paces you.

edits.before: Hold W (Path Maker) for his E pull — unstoppable means the root whiffs and you keep marching in
edits.after: Stay clear of Nevermove's return pass — that half is the root, not the outgoing wave

edits.before: Land E to root you so his W bomb and Q line all connect for free
edits.after: Root you with Nevermove's return so his W bomb and Q line connect free

notes: The whole matchup was built on Path Maker being unstoppable, which Riot's text does not say — that claim is removed rather than reworded, and replaced with Nevermove's return-pass root, which is verifiable from the kit and is the more useful read. Also fixed: the drain was credited to 'Demonic Embrace' (an item) twice instead of Demonic Ascension and Ravenous Flock.
